chunk_findings.detail: The accepted behavior is a success whose note is the fixed text `item is completed; nothing to renew` for a completed, released, or abandoned item. `_no_renewal` never emits that string: a done item gets `item is {gone.state}; nothing to renew` (the `DONE` value, not `completed`), an abandoned item gets `item is abandoned; nothing to renew`, and a released item gets `item has no lease (released); nothing to renew`. A caller or test that matches the decision’s phrase treats all three as a failed or unexpected heartbeat even though nothing was renewed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:_no_renewal

chunk_findings.detail: `merge` does not renew on an interval for the life of the command. It calls `LK.renewer(...)()` once before document refresh and once immediately before `W.merge`, then never again. Given a lease TTL shorter than the landing (the acceptance case: short TTL, ~10-minute run), the last renewal is the instant before `W.merge`; while that call runs the lease still lapses and no further renewal happens until process exit. The knob text even records that `merge` only renews at entry and just before landing, which is not “while they run”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:renew

chunk_findings.detail: `stale_heartbeats` treats any same-uid cmdline that contains the tokens `ddflow` and later `heartbeat` as a heartbeat of whatever first positional `_heartbeat_item` parses, then `heartbeat_notes` tells the operator to `kill` that pid. Given argv `ddflow task comment --body heartbeat T1` (joined cmdline `ddflow task comment --body heartbeat T1`) while `T1` is in `finished`, the regex matches, the item extracted is `T1`, and doctor reports that comment process as a finished-item heartbeat loop. Killing it stops unrelated work; the process never called `heartbeat`.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_heartbeat_on_a_released_open_item_is_a_successful_no_op` rejects the response the governing decision requires. That decision says a heartbeat on a released item returns success with the text `item is completed; nothing to renew` and does not extend the lease. Given `exit == 0`, `reason == "item is completed; nothing to renew"`, and `data == {"renewed": False}` (no `note`), the assertion `"nothing to renew" in str(out.data.get("note", ""))` fails even though nothing was renewed. The completed-item test accepts the same text in `reason`, so the two cases do not lock one contract, and neither asserts the full mandated sentence.

chunk_findings.detail: `renewer` only returns a callable and merge invokes it twice, both before the blocking `W.merge`. Nothing renews on an interval while that call runs, and nothing is stopped when it returns. With a short lease TTL, a merge that takes longer than the TTL (the 10-minute case in the acceptance) lets the lease expire mid-merge; a waiter can take the item or the holder loses it, which is the failure this change was supposed to close. The new test only counts that the spy lambda was called at t=0, so it stays green when the lease dies during `W.merge`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:315

chunk_findings.detail: `_no_renewal` succeeds only when `gone.state` is `DONE` or `ABANDONED`. A released item is neither: claim then release, then `heartbeat` on that id. Control falls through to `L.renew`, which is the old failure (`no lease held`, exit non-zero) or, if a stale lease record is still live, an extension. The contract requires that case to return success and not touch the lease. The new test never releases an item, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:92

chunk_findings.detail: The accepted behavior also requires `doctor` to list heartbeat-looking processes whose item is already finished (pid and command line) and the pkill hook to say how to stop them. This change never touches doctor or that hook. After a finished item, a leftover heartbeat process is invisible to `doctor`, so the operator has no listing to act on.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leasekeep.py:41

chunk_findings.detail: The heartbeat scanner treats a separate flag value as the item id. `_HEARTBEAT` only skips `-\S+` tokens, so `ddflow heartbeat --agent worker T1` (or the same command inside `while true; do ...; done`) captures `worker`, not `T1`. With finished `["T1"]`, `m.group(1) not in done` drops the process and `doctor` never lists pid or command line. The new test only uses `--agent` before the subcommand (`ddflow --agent a heartbeat T1`), so it does not catch this. `ddflow heartbeat --agent=worker T1` still works, which shows the gap is valued options the pattern claims to skip.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:188

chunk_findings.detail: `_HEARTBEAT.search` keeps only the first hit. A leftover loop `while true; do ddflow heartbeat T-live; ddflow heartbeat T1; sleep 60; done` with finished `["T1"]` matches `T-live`, fails the `done` check, and is omitted even though it still heartbeats a finished item. `finditer` over every `ddflow heartbeat` item would list pid 4001; this path returns nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:211

chunk_findings.detail: `_heartbeat_item` splits the shell text on whitespace and, for every name in `_VALUED` (`--reason`, `--repo`, `--agent`), skips only the next token. A leftover loop whose command line is `while true; do ddflow heartbeat --reason "still working" T1; sleep 60; done` (quotes are part of the `sh -c` script in `/proc/.../cmdline`) therefore yields words `--reason`, `"still`, `working"`, `T1`. The skip consumes only `"still`, and the function returns `working` (quotes stripped), not `T1`. With `finished=["T1"]`, `stale_heartbeats` drops pid 4001, so `doctor` never lists the process the pkill hook tells the operator to find there. The same miss happens for a real argv `--reason` / `--repo` value that contains a space, because `" ".join(_argv(...))` erases the argument boundary before the split.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:195

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_HEARTBEAT` pattern is supposed to treat `heartbeat` as the subcommand and not as an option value, but the value group is optional and the engine backtracks into a match. Given the command line `ddflow --reason heartbeat T1` (also `--agent` / `--repo`, the valued globals in `_VALUED`), `\s+-\S+` takes `--reason`, the optional value first consumes `heartbeat`, that attempt fails to find a later subcommand, and backtracking then accepts `heartbeat` as the subcommand with group 1 ` T1`. `stale_heartbeats` therefore lists that process as a heartbeat for T1 even though `heartbeat` is the option value, which is the mis-identification this regex change claims to close. The new test only covers a non-option token (`task`) sitting between `ddflow` and `--body`, so it does not catch this.
